messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Elevated 5xx rate detected in prod (us-west) for prefix-KV tier. Error rate: 18% over last 5m (threshold 5%). Affected frontends: runtime-proxy, model-router. Alert: https://dash.redwood.internal/alerts/3129998888

Alex: ack. I’m oncall and have been paged. Triage starting. @Priya can you join?

Priya: on it. looking at traces and logs now. seeing a lot of gateway timeouts (502/504) and rapid eviction spikes from prefix-cache shards. pulling shard heatmap.

Samir: heatmap shows eviction storm centered on shard-17 and shard-18, eviction rate peaked ~06:10. correlates with recent config change to heartbeat timeout in commit d4c3e2 (deployed 06:12).

Maya: if eviction storm is causing cache misses -> origin thundering at runtime-proxy -> 5xx spikes. We should route around the prefix cache temporarily to stabilize while SRE investigates.

Alex: what's the fastest way to flip routing? Any risk to correctness?

Maya: low correctness risk; fallback path hits KV origin (higher latency). Quick toggle via ops-config API or feature-flag. Runbook excerpt below:

```
# Toggle cache bypass (prod)
POST /ops-api/v1/services/runtime-proxy/config
{
  "env":"prod",
  "overrides": {"ROUTE_PREFIX_CACHE_BYPASS":"true"}
}
```

Samir: I’ll prepare a rolling restart for prefix-cache shard-17 after we flip the bypass. Restart command (k8s):

```
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/prefix-cache-shard-17 -n prod
kubectl logs -f pod/prefix-cache-17-0 -n prod | tail -n 200
```

Priya: doing the bypass now. posting response.

Priya: POST succeeded, feature flag set, runtime-proxy config reload triggered. Observability note: expect latency increase but should reduce 5xx error amplification.

Alex: confirming runbook step: mark incident severity P1 and notify support/public channels. Are there customer reports?

Priya: Support logs show 3 escalations in last 10m and ~120 backend errors recorded in metrics. Two paying customers reported timeouts via Zendesk (tickets #Z-8821 and #Z-8823). Adding to incident ticket.

Samir: starting rolling restart shard-17 now. will coordinate pod drains with health checks.

Samir: restart command issued. monitoring pod restart sequence. health endpoint returning 200 for new pods.

Alex: Observed immediate drop in 5xx from 18% -> 7% in ~3m after bypass flip. Good sign. Keep monitoring while restarts continue.

Priya: digging into eviction cause: logs show frequent "heartbeat lost" errors for shard-17 connections to kv-master. Sample log:

```
WARN prefix-cache: eviction invoked shard=17 key=prefix:user:1234 reason=heartbeat_timeout count=487
ERROR prefix-cache: connection to kv-master node-09 reset during compact
```

Maya: node-09 in that AZ had a noisy neighbor on network link per infra telemetry; infra team flagged packet drops 06:05-06:14. That likely triggered heartbeat timeouts and eviction cascade.

Alex: mitigation plan so far: 1) bypass prefix-cache routing (done), 2) restart affected prefix-cache shards (in progress), 3) monitor 5xx and customer impact, 4) infra to investigate network flakiness and repair node-09.

Morgan: I’m coming oncall at 17:45 UTC — taking handoff. Current state: bypass=true, shard-17 restart in progress, 5xx down to ~3-5% and trending down. Customer tickets opened and acknowledged by support.

Alex: handing off to @Morgan. notes: suspect heartbeat timeout regression from recent config change; SRE to rollback heartbeat tweak if infra can't guarantee stable links. Also follow-up: add circuit-breaker on runtime-proxy to limit origin thundering when cache misses spike.

Morgan: acknowledged. I’ll keep monitoring for 1h, coordinate with infra for node remediation, and update incident ticket INC-4321.

OpsBot: autoscaler: runtime-proxy scaled +4 pods to handle increased origin load (triggered at 06:18).

Alex: thanks team. leaving channel. :thumbsup:

Priya: will capture timeline and post a short post-incident summary once we have infra RCA.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-4321 created and labeled P1 — incident channel: #inc-4321.

Morgan: final note before I take watch — continuing to monitor error budget and support queues. If 5xx creeps back above 5% re-escalate immediately.
